notes: Travel banter between two companions (PLAN-LEVELING.md 8; game/banter.h). The engine's own writing. Characters: docs/companion_personalities.md; all of it in one place: docs/banter_review.md (tools/banter_doc.py).

pairs: each unordered pair of companion ids once; mood is for the review only. exchanges play in file order, each once per save; repeat (the 'run out of things to say' joke) only when every exchange of every present pair is heard, one time in three a point fires.
A line is {"<companion id>": "<text>"}; {avatar} = the Avatar's name. Optional per exchange: when: {step_done: [...], step_not_done: [...]} (critical-path step ids).

lines.kalvax: Morvain, dost thou ever smile, or would it crack thy face?

lines.morvain: I smiled once. At a funeral. It was a very good funeral.

lines.kalvax: Of course it was.

lines.morvain: Thou flinchest when I speak of burial, sorcerer.

lines.kalvax: I do not flinch. I simply prefer to go out in a blaze.

lines.morvain: Fire leaves nothing to bury. No stone, no name. Only ash on the wind.

lines.kalvax: Then they will have to remember me some other way. Loudly.
Thy skeleton swung at a troll and lost its own arm.

lines.morvain: It was a hundred years old. What didst thou do at a hundred years old?

lines.kalvax: I intend to be a god by then.

lines.morvain: Then I will dig thee a very large hole.
Thou didst stand very close to the Avatar in that last fight.

lines.kalvax: To aim better.

lines.morvain: Mm. I stand near the living when I am afraid too.

lines.kalvax: Say that again and I will set thy hood alight.
Say something, gravedigger.

lines.morvain: Something.

lines.kalvax: Pyros give me strength.

lines.brannoc: Thou walkest like a man following a coffin.

lines.morvain: I am. Usually someone else's. Today, thine. I am measuring.

lines.brannoc: Measuring what?

lines.morvain: Thou wilt need a long hole. They stretch.
Thou didst hold thy breath all through the catacombs, Brannoc.

lines.brannoc: Low roofs. No wind. Feels like being buried.

lines.morvain: It is very peaceful, being buried.

lines.brannoc: Then thou canst have my turn.
Rain soon.

lines.morvain: The ground will be soft. Good digging.

lines.brannoc: That's not what I meant.

lines.morvain: It is what I meant.

lines.varn: Thou servest Lithos and I serve Hydros. Our gods are seldom friends.

lines.morvain: Our gods quarrel. Their servants need not.

lines.varn: Well said. An oath to one is still an oath.

lines.morvain: And a grave dug for anyone is still a grave dug well.
Thou washest thy blade in every stream we pass, warden.

lines.varn: A warden's habit. Blood should go back to the water.

lines.morvain: I wash the dead before they go into the earth. It is much the same.

lines.varn: Then we both send something home.
The water is high today.

lines.morvain: The ground is low today.

lines.varn: ...That is not a conversation.

lines.morvain: No. But it passed the time.

lines.ilvaran: Dost thou pray for the dead thou buriest, Morvain?

lines.morvain: I sing to them. Lithos does not care for prayers. He likes a good tune.

lines.ilvaran: Then perhaps I will learn one. For the Zealans.

lines.morvain: They are long past my hearing. But I will teach thee anyway.
Thou thankest every creature thou killest.

lines.ilvaran: Someone should. They did not ask to be born angry.

lines.morvain: Nor did I. I am thankful nobody killed me for it.

lines.ilvaran: What a peaceful road.

lines.morvain: Like a cemetery.

lines.ilvaran: I did not mean it like that.

lines.morvain: I did.

lines.corvin: So, Morvain. Hypothetically. Do the dead ever take rings with them?

lines.morvain: Hypothetically, yes. And hypothetically, I bury thieves too.

lines.corvin: Just asking. For a friend.

lines.morvain: Thy friend would make a fine short grave.
Thou gavest that beggar in Tenebrae a coin and thoughtest nobody saw.

lines.corvin: Didn't happen. And if it did, it was a bad coin.

lines.morvain: The dead see everything, Corvin.

lines.corvin: Then the dead can keep their mouths shut. They're good at that.
Why dost thou always walk behind me?

lines.morvain: So I can see thy hands.

lines.corvin: Fair. I would do the same.
Morvain. Morvain. Thou'rt very quiet.

lines.morvain: So are the dead.

lines.corvin: I knew thou'd say that.

lines.wynna: Morvain, what do the dead actually say? When thou listenest?

lines.morvain: Mostly that they are cold. And that I dig too slowly.

lines.wynna: That's it? No secrets of the ages?

lines.morvain: Thou wouldst be surprised how much of the ages is complaining.
Thou countest the skulls in every catacomb we enter.

lines.wynna: Eighty-one in the last hall! Well, eighty, one was a pot.

lines.morvain: Count softer. Some of them were friends.
Must I?

lines.nerissa: Thou hearest the ground the way I hear the sea.

lines.morvain: The ground mutters. Thy sea sings, I think.

lines.nerissa: She weeps more than she sings.

lines.morvain: Then we both keep sad company. It suits us.
Thou didst pick up a shell back there, and kiss it.

lines.nerissa: Something lived in it once. It deserves a kindness.

lines.morvain: Thou wouldst have made a good gravekeeper.

lines.nerissa: Perhaps I am one. The sea's.

lines.morvain: Quiet.

lines.nerissa: Yes.

lines.morvain: Good.

lines.kalvax: Brannoc, what dost thou want? Power? Gold? A throne?

lines.brannoc: Open ground and a good meal.

lines.kalvax: That is the saddest thing I have ever heard.

lines.brannoc: Thou hast not heard thyself snore.
Thou didst cast three bolts at a ghoul that was already falling.

lines.kalvax: I wanted to be sure.

lines.brannoc: Thou didst want everyone to watch.

lines.kalvax: ...Both things can be true.
Talk, axe-man. I am bored.

lines.brannoc: Wind's from the west.

lines.kalvax: Talk about something else.

lines.brannoc: Wind's from the west, still.

lines.varn: Thou servest a Titan who would burn this land to its roots.

lines.kalvax: And thou servest one who would drown it. At least mine is quick.

lines.varn: Hydros feeds the land. Pyros only eats it.

lines.kalvax: Fire clears the dead wood, warden. Even thou art a little dead wood.
Thou keepest walking between me and every puddle, Varn.

lines.varn: Thou keepest stepping round them like a cat.

lines.kalvax: I do not like getting my boots wet. That is all.

lines.varn: The water will not hurt thee, sorcerer. Not unless thou fall in.

lines.kalvax: Thank thee. Very comforting.

lines.varn: Thou didst laugh when that creature burned.

lines.kalvax: It was trying to eat me. I am allowed to laugh.

lines.varn: A warden does not laugh at a death.

lines.kalvax: Then it is lucky I am not a warden. One of us should enjoy his work.
Water, water, everywhere.

lines.varn: Fire, fire, nowhere.

lines.kalvax: Thou practised that.

lines.ilvaran: May I ask thee something, Kalvax?

lines.kalvax: If it is about my soul, no.

lines.ilvaran: It was about thy hands. They shake after thou castest.

lines.kalvax: They are cold. Fire leaves them cold. Mind thine own hands, pilgrim.
Thou didst pray over that ghoul. It was a ghoul.

lines.ilvaran: It was someone, once.

lines.kalvax: Now it is ash. I made sure.

lines.ilvaran: Then I will pray for the ash too. It costs me nothing.

lines.kalvax: It costs me my patience.
Thy gods left, Ilvaran. Mine is still burning. Who is the fool?

lines.ilvaran: Perhaps both of us. I hope they are listening. Thou hopest he is not.

lines.kalvax: ...I said no talk about souls.

lines.ilvaran: Thou didst. I am sorry.
Peace be with thee, Kalvax.

lines.kalvax: It never is.

lines.ilvaran: I will keep saying it.

lines.corvin: So what's thy plan, Kalvax? After all this?

lines.kalvax: A tower. Disciples. My old master licking ash off my floor.

lines.corvin: Modest. I just want a house with a lock nobody can pick.

lines.kalvax: Thou couldst pick it.

lines.corvin: Aye, that's the beauty of it.

lines.kalvax: Thou art the only one here who understands wanting more, thief.

lines.corvin: I understand wanting more. I also understand getting caught.

lines.kalvax: I do not get caught. I get exiled.

lines.corvin: Same thing with a nicer view.
Burn anything good lately?

lines.kalvax: Thee, soon.

lines.corvin: Lovely chat.

lines.wynna: Kalvax, how hot is a fire bolt? Exactly? In numbers?

lines.kalvax: Hot enough.
It is a sorcerer's number.
Thy lightning was showy back there. Clumsy, but showy.
It was a warning shot. Twice.

lines.wynna: Mythran says that, too, when he misses.
Kalvax, why dost thou never ask the Avatar about his world?

lines.kalvax: Because I will rule this one first, and then ask.
It is ambitious. Thou wouldst not understand.
I did not say anything.
Stop looking at me like that, sea-girl.

lines.nerissa: Like what?

lines.kalvax: Like thou knowest how I end.

lines.nerissa: I do not. The sea says nothing of thee. I think thou art too warm for her.

lines.kalvax: ...Good.

lines.nerissa: Thou walkest far from the shore whenever we are near the water.

lines.kalvax: The view is better from up here.

lines.nerissa: She would not take thee, Kalvax. She takes only what falls.

lines.kalvax: Then I will not fall. Talk of something else.
Any prophecies today?

lines.nerissa: Rain.

lines.kalvax: There is always rain.

lines.nerissa: Then I am always right.

lines.varn: Thou fightest well, Brannoc. Thou shouldst have been a warden.

lines.brannoc: Too many prayers. I'd forget the words.

lines.varn: The water does not mind the words. Only the heart.

lines.brannoc: Then maybe. When I'm old. And slow.
Thou dost keep thy shield up even walking. Waiting for something?

lines.varn: Always. A warden is never off his watch.

lines.brannoc: Tiring, that.

lines.varn: Yes. But someone must stand still while the rest of thee run.

lines.brannoc: Wind.

lines.varn: Water.

lines.brannoc: Glad we sorted that.

lines.ilvaran: Thou hearest Stratos better than any theurgist I have known.

lines.brannoc: I don't hear her. I just smell the rain.

lines.ilvaran: That is how she speaks to most of us. Few listen.

lines.brannoc: Well, I'm listening now. She says hurry up.
Thou walkest slow, pilgrim. Every stone, thou stoppest.

lines.ilvaran: Someone walked here before us. I like to say hello.

lines.brannoc: I'd like to get there before dark.

lines.ilvaran: We will. And we will have said hello.
A blessed day.

lines.brannoc: Windy.

lines.ilvaran: Blessedly windy.

lines.corvin: Brannoc, mate, thy purse is hanging out.

lines.brannoc: I know. I'm watching thee watch it.

lines.corvin: ...Respect.

lines.brannoc: Thou didst back off in that last fight, Crow. Quick, too.

lines.corvin: Strategic. I go round, they don't see me coming.

lines.brannoc: They didn't see thee at all.

lines.corvin: Exactly! Working as intended.
Nice axe.

lines.brannoc: Thou saidst that yesterday.

lines.corvin: Still nice.

lines.wynna: Brannoc, how does thy knee know about rain? Is it magic? Can I touch it?

lines.brannoc: No.

lines.wynna: Is that no, it isn't magic, or no, I can't touch it?

lines.brannoc: Yes.
Thou didst run the whole way up that hill, girl. Not even out of breath.

lines.wynna: I talk while I run. It trains the lungs.

lines.brannoc: That explains a lot.
...Aye. Go.
Rain.

lines.nerissa: Storm by dark.

lines.brannoc: Aye. Coming over the hills. Thou didst smell it too?

lines.nerissa: I heard it, in the water underground.

lines.brannoc: Huh. My knee and thy water. Between us we'd make a fine stormwatch.
Thou dost not like towns either, dost thou?

lines.nerissa: Too many voices. I cannot hear her.

lines.brannoc: Too many walls. I cannot breathe.

lines.nerissa: Then let us walk faster, out of here.

lines.brannoc: Rain soon.

lines.nerissa: Rain soon.

lines.brannoc: Glad we agree.

lines.ilvaran: Thou prayest as thou walkest, Varn. What dost thou ask for?

lines.varn: Not to break my oath today.

lines.ilvaran: Only today?

lines.varn: Tomorrow I will ask again. One day at a time is how oaths are kept.
Thy gods are gone, pilgrim, and thou kneelest still. Why?

lines.ilvaran: Because they might not be gone. And if they are, I would rather be found kneeling.

lines.varn: That is how I feel of Hydros some days.

lines.ilvaran: Then we are not so different, thou and I.

lines.varn: Shall we pray?

lines.ilvaran: We prayed an hour ago.

lines.varn: Shall we pray again?

lines.ilvaran: ...Yes, all right.

lines.varn: Thy hand was near that merchant's belt, Corvin.

lines.corvin: Was it? I was stretching.

lines.varn: Stretch the other way.

lines.corvin: Warden, dost thou ever do anything wrong? Ever? Once?

lines.varn: Yes. Every day I fall short of my oath.

lines.corvin: That's not what I meant. I meant fun wrong.

lines.varn: I know what thou didst mean.
Thou didst turn thy face away at the dock, when we passed the block.

lines.corvin: Bad smell. Fish.

lines.varn: It was not the fish.

lines.corvin: ...Drop it, warden. Please.
Still watching me?

lines.varn: Yes.

lines.corvin: Good. I'd hate to be ignored.

lines.wynna: Varn, dost thou ever laugh? I've been counting. Zero times.

lines.varn: I laughed in my youth.
I no longer remember. That is probably why I stopped.
Thou shouldst not run ahead, child. The road has teeth.

lines.wynna: I'm not a child! I'm twenty-three. Ish.

lines.varn: Then run ahead carefully, woman of twenty-three-ish.

lines.wynna: Ha! That was nearly a joke!

lines.varn: The day is not over.
No.
Thou hearest her, Nerissa. Truly hearest her.

lines.nerissa: Only moods. Thou servest her. That is harder.

lines.varn: Serving is easy. Hearing is what I lack.

lines.nerissa: I will tell thee what she says, when she says something kind.
Thou dost stand between me and every foe. Every time.

lines.varn: A warden guards the tide's own. I count thee among them.

lines.nerissa: I can step back by myself, Varn.

lines.varn: I know. Let me do it anyway.
The rains have been too heavy. Does she say why?

lines.nerissa: She dreams badly. Something holds her down.

lines.varn: I feel it too, at the lake. Like a breath held too long.

lines.nerissa: Then we feel the same thing. That is some comfort.
The water is calm.

lines.varn: Good.

lines.nerissa: Thou always sayest that.

lines.varn: It is always good.

lines.corvin: Ilvaran, stop looking at me like I'm a stray dog thou wantest to feed.

lines.ilvaran: Art thou hungry?

lines.corvin: ...A little. That's not the point.

lines.ilvaran: Here. Bread. It is the point.
Thou art kinder than thou wishest to seem, Corvin.

lines.corvin: Lies. Slander. I'm a terrible person.

lines.ilvaran: I saw thee carry that child's bucket in Tenebrae.

lines.corvin: She was slow. I was in a hurry. That's all.

lines.ilvaran: Bless thee, Corvin.

lines.corvin: Stop that.

lines.ilvaran: Bless thee anyway.

lines.wynna: Ilvaran, what did the Zealans eat? Nobody ever says.

lines.ilvaran: I do not know. Bread, I hope. Bread is holy everywhere.

lines.wynna: I'll find out. There must be a book.

lines.ilvaran: If there is, read it to me. Slowly.
Thou laughest at danger, Wynna. Even when thou art hurt.

lines.wynna: If I stop laughing I'll have to think about it.

lines.ilvaran: Then laugh. I will do the thinking for us both.
This stone.

lines.nerissa: The tide knows thy name, Ilvaran. I hear it sometimes, when I sleep.

lines.ilvaran: Then if I fall, I know who will call me back.

lines.nerissa: I would rather not have to.

lines.ilvaran: So would I. Let us both be careful.
Thou art sad today, Nerissa.

lines.nerissa: The sea is sad. I only carry it.

lines.ilvaran: Then let me carry some. I have room.

lines.nerissa: ...Thank thee. A little, then.

lines.ilvaran: Peace.

lines.nerissa: Peace.

lines.ilvaran: That was nice.

lines.wynna: Corvin, didst thou take a book from that house back there?

lines.corvin: Borrowed. Same as thy library book.
Mine's for the pictures. Also scholarship.
Wynna, thou'rt a terrible lookout. Thou wavest at the guards.
They looked armed.

lines.wynna: Lonely and armed. The worst combination.
Corvin, teach me to pick a lock. Please?

lines.corvin: Thou wouldst talk to the lock and tell it everything.

lines.wynna: Maybe it would open out of sympathy!

lines.corvin: Do not make me laugh in the middle of a heist.
Nothing.
Nothing thou hast noticed.
Nerissa. Thou keepest looking at my hands.

lines.nerissa: They stopped moving. When thou standest near me, they stop.

lines.corvin: Do they? Huh. That's... unsettling.

lines.nerissa: I think they are resting.
Thou leavest coins on the dock steps when no one is looking.

lines.corvin: Who told thee that?

lines.nerissa: The water. Coins fall in, sometimes.

lines.corvin: Clumsy of me. Don't tell anyone.
Seen anything about me lately?

lines.nerissa: Thou wilt trip.

lines.corvin: When?

lines.nerissa: Soon.

lines.wynna: Nerissa, what does Hydros sound like? Exactly?

lines.nerissa: Like someone humming in the next room.
I have never known. I hope one day she sings the words.
Thou talkest so much, Wynna.
No. Don't. It is like rain on a roof. I like it.
Something.

lines.wynna: Morvain taught thee that, didn't he?
